scenes.vo: An exchange is a company that lets you swap your normal money (dollars, pounds, euros) for crypto. It's your on-ramp. Choose one that is: Well-known examples include Coinbase, Kraken, Binance, Bybit and OKX, but availability differs by country. Pick one that's legally available to you. You'll be asked for K.Y.C. ("know your customer"): ID and sometimes proof of address. This is normal and legally required for regulated exchanges. Secure it before depositing: Licensed or registered where you live (check your country's financial regulator) Large and long-established, with a good security record Supports your bank's deposit method and the coins/networks you'll use (ETH, U.S.D.C., and low-cost networks such as Arbitrum or Base) Unique, long password stored in a password manager (for example Bitwarden, 1Password) Secure your email first. Whoever controls your email can often reset your exchange account. Give it its own strong password and two-factor.
scenes.cap: Licensed or registered where you live (check your country's financial regulator) Large and long-established, with a good security record Supports your bank's deposit method and the coins/networks you'll use (ETH, USDC, and low-cost networks such as Arbitrum or Base) Unique, long password stored in a password manager (e.g. Bitwarden, 1Password) Secure your email first. Whoever controls your email can often reset your exchange account. Give it its own strong password and 2FA.

scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Two-factor authentication (2FA) with an authenticator app (e.g. Google Authenticator,…
Save the 2FA backup codes offline (on paper, stored safely)
Turn on the anti-phishing code if offered (a word that appears in every real email from…
Turn on the withdrawal address allowlist if offered (withdrawals can only go to…
scenes.vo: Two-factor authentication (two-factor) with an authenticator app (for example Google Authenticator, Authy) or a hardware security key. Avoid SMS codes: phone numbers can be hijacked ("SIM swap"). Save the two-factor backup codes offline (on paper, stored safely) Turn on the anti-phishing code if offered (a word that appears in every real email from the exchange) Turn on the withdrawal address allowlist if offered (withdrawals can only go to addresses you pre-approved)

lines: Why secure your email before the exchange?
scenes.sub: Answer: Email is often how accounts are reset. Whoever controls it can take over the exchange account.
